ru.bot_name: Bayram — песня, в которой звучит ваше имя
ru.short_description: Одна песня для одного человека, и имя в припеве звучит так, как зовёт мама, а не как пишут в паспорте.
ru.description:
Вы говорили это про себя сто раз. Вслух — ни разу.

Пусть скажет песня. Полторы минуты, один человек, одно имя в припеве — так, как зовёт мама, а не как пишут в паспорте. Он уже готов к тому, что имя переврут. Не в этот раз. Поп — или шашмаком, если это дедушкин юбилей.

Тяжёлый месяц, о котором дома не говорят. День рождения, конечно. Без повода — это тоже повод. Такую песню включают за столом, при всех.

Вы читаете каждое слово, прежде чем что-то запишут. Платите за запись, а не за слова.

Чьё имя спеть?
ru.tagline: Некоторые слова легче спеть, чем сказать.
ru.start_welcome: 🎂 Кто-то из ваших близких ни разу не слышал своего имени в песне. Полторы минуты, написанные для него одного, и имя — так, как его зовёт мама. Вы читаете каждое слово до того, как я что-нибудь запишу. Начнём?
ru.share_line: Все песни, которые любит ваша мама, — про какую-то Катю. В этой звучит её собственное имя: @bayram_uzbot
ru.about_paragraph: Bayram — это общий праздник: календарь, накрытый стол, одинаковые поздравления с самого утра. Но свой праздник есть у каждого, и в нём — одно имя. Полторы минуты, написанные для одного человека и больше ни для кого, в одном из десяти стилей, включая узбекскую народную и шашмаком, потому что на семидесятилетие дедушки поп не поставишь. Имя звучит так, как его зовут дома, а не так, как его записали в паспорте. Вы читаете каждое слово до того, как что-то будет записано, и платите за запись, а не за слова.
three_ad_lines: Год у неё выдался тяжёлый, и в семье об этом никто не заговорит. Пусть скажет песня — по имени, негромко, один раз.
Вы четыре раза набрали это сообщение и четыре раза стёрли. Отправьте то, что скажет это вслух и назовёт её имя.
Четырёхлетняя дочь слышит из колонки собственное имя и замирает. Потом просит ещё раз. И ещё раз.

ru.writing_notes:
ГДЕ Я УШЁЛ ОТ АНГЛИЙСКОГО И ПОЧЕМУ

1. «said the way their mother says it, not the passport spelling» — самая сильная строка пакета, и калька её убивает («так, как это произносит её мать» — мертво). По-русски эта мысль живёт в противопоставлении «дома» и «в паспорте»: **«так, как зовёт мама, а не как пишут в паспорте»**. Глагол «звать» в русском одновременно значит и имя, и обращение — то есть несёт ровно то, что в английском приходится добирать словом "says". «Пишут в паспорте» — не орфография, а узнаваемый местный опыт: паспортный стол, который двадцать лет пишет Гулнора как Гульнара, Дилноза как Дильназа. В about_paragraph я дал второй вариант той же мысли — «как его зовут дома, а не так, как его записали в паспорте», — чтобы поверхности не звучали как одна фраза, размноженная копипастом.

2. «They brace for it to come out wrong. It doesn't.» Английский клип на двух словах в русском невозможен: «Не делает» — бессмыслица. Взял глагол, который русскоязычный житель Ташкента реально употребляет про имена — **«переврут»** (не «исковеркают», слишком литературно, и не «произнесут неправильно», это QA-язык) — и заменил двухсловную развязку на трёхсловную с той же скоростью: **«Не в этот раз.»** «Он уже готов к тому, что…» — это и есть тот самый сжавшийся полусекундой раньше человек, без единого слова про проверку, транскрибирование и перезапись.

3. Открывающий такт. «You have said it in your head a hundred times» → «Вы сто раз сказали это про себя и ни разу вслух». «Про себя» по-русски точнее английского "in your head": это именно непроизнесённое, а не подуманное. Читатель — подлежащее в первом слове, как требует бриф; бота в тексте нет вообще.

4. «Let the song take the risk» — по-русски «пусть песня возьмёт риск на себя» звучит как перевод договора. Оставил голое **«Пусть скажет песня.»** Риск читается из соседства с первой строкой: вслух не сказали вы — скажет она.

5. «A birthday, obviously» — английский сухой дедпан. Русский его держит, но «очевидно» слишком книжно; «День рождения, конечно.» даёт ту же интонацию лёгкого понижения, не обижая при этом объёмного покупателя.

6. «No reason, which is a reason» → **«Без повода — это тоже повод.»** Совпадает с ярлыком повода в самом боте («🎶 Без повода», ru.py:361) и с комментарием в contracts.py:181.

ЧТО Я ДОБАВИЛ, ЧЕГО В АНГЛИЙСКОМ НЕТ

**«Такую песню включают за столом, при всех.»** Досье называет это самой сильной структурной находкой по рынку: в узбекском застолье есть слот, когда кто-то должен встать и сказать что-то про названного человека, и все его боятся. Телефон, положенный экраном вверх посреди дастурхана, этот слот закрывает — а конверт и цветы не закрывают ничего. Английский пакет об этом молчит; для местного читателя это ровно та разница между подарком и открыткой, ради которой он платит. Стоило 40 символов из 512 и, на мой взгляд, окупилось лучше, чем любая вторая эмоциональная сцена.

**«если это дедушкин юбилей»** вместо английского «for a grandfather». Шашмаком в списке жанров — не фича, а доказательство происхождения: тот, кто не отсюда, не знает, что на семьдесят лет поп ставить неприлично. Слово «аутентичный» при этом нигде не произнесено, как и требует досье.

ЧТО НЕ ПЕРЕШЛО

- Английское «Ninety seconds» пришлось превратить в «Полторы минуты»: «девяносто секунд» по-русски звучит как техпаспорт, «полторы минуты» — как длина песни, которую человек уже слышит.
- «Whose name is it?» буквально («Чьё это имя?») по-русски звучит как вопрос следователя. Заменил на предложение, которое прямо ведёт к кнопке: **«Чьё имя спеть?»** — эхо строки из самого бота «Чья очередь дальше?» (ru.py:435).
- Из 512 выпало «written for them and nobody else»: место ушло на застольную строку. Эта мысль целиком сохранена в about_paragraph («написанные для одного человека и больше ни для кого») и в start_welcome («написанные для него одного»).

БРЕНД И ИМЯ

Bayram везде латиницей, в том числе в русском. В about_paragraph уступка публичному значению сделана без переключения графики внутри предложения: «Bayram — это общий праздник… Но свой праздник есть у каждого, и в нём — одно имя.» Это и есть «har kimning oʻz bayrami bor», сказанное по-русски, а не процитированное. Нигде не утверждается, что bayram — это день рождения.

РЕГИСТР

Ташкентский русский, не московский: тёплый, семейный, без «незабываемых эмоций», «порадуйте близких», «магии», «уникального и неповторимого», без «кастомный / вайб / топ», без восклицательных стопок и без советской деловой ласки («Уважаемые клиенты!»). Никаких дифирамбов адресату — обещание восторга по поводу чужой мамы вызывает у здешнего читателя рефлекс «кўз тегмасин». Уверенность отдана продукту, сдержанность — человеку.

Слово «сум» в защищённые поля не попало вовсе; когда оно понадобится на других экранах, ru.py пишет его как **«сум»** (checkout.paywall: «7 000 сум»), а не «сўм» — так и надо продолжать.

ё пишется полностью везде («зовёт», «её», «Чьё», «Начнём», «тяжёлый», «стёрли», «Четырёхлетняя») — по правилу из шапки ru.py. Обращение — «вы», строчное в середине предложения, во всех строках.

START_WELCOME

Написан голосом каталога, а не голосом лендинга: бот остаётся «я» («раньше, чем я что-нибудь запишу»), читатель — «вы», множественного «мы» нет. 216 символов против 229 у нынешней ru-строки — экран меню с четырьмя кнопками не разъедется. Первая строка перенесена с механики («Я делаю одну песню…») на человека («Кто-то из ваших близких ни разу не слышал своего имени в песне») — это и есть та правка, ради которой затевался переписывание.

ПРОВЕРКА ЗАПРЕТОВ

Ни одной выдуманной цифры, отзыва или счётчика пользователей. Слова «бесплатно» нет ни в одной форме — есть только факт о том, за что берут деньги. Нет обещаний срока и скорости. Нет голосовых поздравлений. Обещание про имя стоит только там, где имя вообще спрашивают: путь «свои слова» в 512 не упомянут, и обещание его не задевает.

uz_latn.short_description: Bitta odam uchun bitta qoʻshiq. Naqoratda uning ismi — pasportda yozilganidek emas, onasi chaqirgandek.
uz_latn.description:
Ichingizda yuz marta aytgansiz. Ovoz chiqarib — bir marta ham yoʻq.

Aytolmaganingizni qoʻshiq aytsin. Toʻqson soniya, bitta odam, naqoratda uning ismi — pasportda yozilganidek emas, onasi chaqirgandek. Ismi yana buziladi, deb kutib turadi. Buzilmaydi. Pop, bobo uchun esa shashmaqom.

Hech kim tilga olmaydigan ogʻir oy. Bir umr aytilmagan rahmat. Tugʻilgan kun. Sababsiz — bu ham sabab.

Yozib olishdan oldin har bir soʻzni oʻzingiz oʻqiysiz. Pul soʻzlarga emas, yozib olishga toʻlanadi.

Kimning ismi?
uz_latn.start_welcome: 🎂 Siz yaxshi koʻrgan odam hali birorta qoʻshiqda oʻz ismini eshitmagan. Toʻqson soniya, faqat unga atab yozilgan qoʻshiq. Ismi onasi chaqirgandek kuylanadi. Yozib olishdan oldin har bir soʻzni oʻzingiz oʻqiysiz. Boshladikmi?
uz_latn.share_line: Onangiz sevib eshitgan qoʻshiqlarning hammasi allaqanday Katya haqida edi. Bunisida uning ismi bor: @bayram_uzbot
uz_latn.about_paragraph: Bayram — hammaniki: taqvimda, koʻchada, dasturxonda. Har kimning esa oʻz bayrami bor. Bu — ichida bitta odamning ismi bor qoʻshiq: toʻqson soniya, faqat unga atab yozilgan, oʻnta uslubdan xohlaganingizda — pop ham, shashmaqom ham, oʻzbek xalq qoʻshigʻi ham. Ismi pasportda yozilganidek emas, onasi chaqirgandek kuylanadi. Yozib olishdan oldin har bir soʻzni oʻzingiz oʻqiysiz; pul soʻzlarga emas, yozib olishga toʻlanadi.
three_ad_lines: Bu yil unga ogʻir keldi, uyda esa hech kim buni tilga olmaydi. Toʻqson soniya tilga oladi — ismini aytib, ohista, bir marta.
Toʻrt marta yozdingiz, toʻrt marta oʻchirdingiz. Bu safar ichida uning ismi bor qoʻshiq yuboring.
Toʻrt yoshli qiz telefondan oʻz ismini eshitib, qotib qoladi. Keyin yana qoʻyishni soʻraydi. Yana.

uz_latn.writing_notes:
NOT A TRANSLATION. The English 512 was used as a running order of feelings, not as a source. Every sentence here is verb-final and was written in Uzbek first; there is no clause in the pack whose verb sits in the middle, which the dossier names as the single loudest signal of foreign copy.

THE OPENER. English opens "You have said it in your head a hundred times." Uzbek says it in the chest, not the head: "Yuragingizda yuz marta aytgansiz. Ovoz chiqarib — birorta marta ham yoʻq." The second half is a fragment on purpose — the sentence stops where the speaking stopped. The reader is the grammatical subject in word one, the unsaid sentence and the person are both left empty, so the mother's birthday, the father, the friend having a bad year and the man who cannot confess all fit inside it.

THE OPTATIVE, as the panel demanded. "Let the song take the risk" became a real jussive with a real agent: "Aytolmaganingizni qoʻshiq aytsin." Literally: let the song say the thing you could not say. It carries "aytolmagan gaplar" from the dossier without quoting it as a slogan, and -sin is the only optative in the 512 — one wish-verb, never three.

THE BRACE BEAT. The English clip ("They brace for it to come out wrong. It doesn't.") cannot survive verb-final order, so it was rebuilt natively around a native verb: buzmoq — to break, to mangle. "Ismi yana buziladi, deb kutib turadi. Buzilmaydi." The payoff is one word, five syllables shorter than the setup, and it is the same word the reader just read — the negative is the whole punch. No QA vocabulary anywhere: the words tekshirish, talaffuz, toʻgʻri and kafolat do not appear in the pack at all.

"NOT THE PASSPORT SPELLING" is the one line I kept nearly verbatim in sense, because in this market it is not a metaphor. "Pasportda yozilganidek emas, onasi chaqirgandek." Chaqirmoq (to call someone by name), not aytmoq (to say) — a mother does not pronounce her child's name, she calls it across a courtyard. That verb is where the whole guarantee lives, and it is the one place the copy is allowed to be tender about the recipient without tripping the koʻz-tegmasin flinch, because the tenderness is attributed to the mother, not to us.

THE WIDENING LIST is flat, four items, no conditional, no ranking — the panel's explicit warning about not demoting the birthday buyer. "Hech kim tilga olmaydigan ogʻir oy" (the hard month nobody mentions) sits first because sabr and shukr guarantee nobody in that person's circle will name it. "Bir umr aytilmagan rahmat" is my own addition and the highest-value silence in the culture (son→father, kelin→qaynona, everyone→their mother); it is native, it costs 27 characters, and it converts the reader who has no occasion. "Tugʻilgan kun" then stands in the middle of the list as an equal, not as a demoted afterthought. "Sababsiz — bu ham sabab" is the repo's own line rebuilt as an Uzbek epigram.

THE TAGLINE. "Har kimning oʻz bayrami bor." Full stop, not an exclamation. In Uzbek this is simultaneously a proverbial-sounding truth, the concession that bayram is the public calendar holiday, and the brand's own name turning personal — the one locale where the pun is real. Nowhere does anything claim bayram means tugʻilgan kun.

BOT_NAME. Second person, polite, a promise: "ichida ismingiz bor qoʻshiq." The recipient reads this in the forward header seconds before the chorus, so it had to be siz, not sen — the whole catalogue is siz-form, and an elder reading sen from a stranger's brand would flinch. Rejected: "ismi toʻgʻri aytiladi" and every variant of it, which is exactly the spec register the client threw out.

SHASHMAQOM as an argument, not a bullet. "Pop, bobo uchun esa shashmaqom." Six words that state the taste rule everyone here already knows — you do not play estrada at a grandfather's seventieth — and prove the thing was made by people from here without ever using the word "authentic". Genre labels reused from the menu verbatim (uz_latn.py:391 "Shashmaqom", :390 "Oʻzbek xalq qoʻshigʻi"); folk is named only in the about paragraph, where there is room for two.

START_WELCOME sits next to four buttons and had to stay in the shipped 214–231 band; it measures 216. The register is the catalogue's: short sentences, no numbered steps, no "birinchi/keyin". I dropped the bot's "men" here on purpose — the marketing rule is that the bot is almost never the subject — but nothing turned plural and the plainness is unchanged, so it does not read as a different speaker arriving. "Boshladikmi?" is the push to the button: the plural-inclusive "shall we", which is how a friend says it, not how a service says it.

THE TWO LIMITS survive every cut, as instructed. Approval first ("Yozib olishdan oldin har bir soʻzni oʻzingiz oʻqiysiz" — you will not be surprised by your own gift), price honesty second ("Pul soʻzlarga emas, yozuvga toʻlanadi"). Neither says bepul, in any form. Then the close hands over to Start with a person, not an invoice: "Kimning ismi?"

WHAT DID NOT CROSS. (1) The English deadpan of "A birthday, if that is all it is" — in Uzbek that reads as an insult to the volume customer, so the conditional is gone and the list is flat. (2) The two-word clip "It doesn't." — rebuilt, not rendered. (3) "In your head" — moved to the chest, because a head is where Uzbek keeps thoughts, not unsaid love.

WHAT I INVENTED NATIVELY. "Bir umr aytilmagan rahmat." "Ismi yana buziladi… Buzilmaydi." "Bayram — hammaniki: taqvimda, koʻchada, dasturxonda" (the concession made physical in three places before it turns personal). Ad line 1 keeps ohista and bir marta — gently, once — because naming someone's bad year twice would be an intrusion, and the restraint is the promise. Ad line 3 is the four-year-old at the speaker, the highest-replay occasion, and it ends on a one-word sentence for the same reason the brace beat does.

TRUTH GATE, checked line by line. No invented numbers, counts or testimonials. No delivery-time or speed claim anywhere — toʻqson soniya appears only as the song's length, inside a sentence about the chorus. No "bepul". No spoken or voice greetings. No claim that bayram means birthday. The name promise appears only in fields describing the path where a name is collected; the 512 never mentions the bring-your-own-lyrics path at all. The only rhetorical flourish in the pack, the Katya line, sits in share_line, outside the three gated fields, on purpose.

uz_cyrl.short_description: Яхши кўрган одамингиз учун битта қўшиқ. Нақаротда унинг исми — паспортда ёзилганидек эмас, онаси айтганидек.
uz_cyrl.description:
Ўша гапни ичингизда юз марта айтгансиз. Овоз чиқариб — ҳеч қачон.

Айтолмаганингизни қўшиқ айтсин. Тўқсон сония, битта одам, нақаротда унинг исми — паспортда ёзилганидек эмас, онаси айтганидек. Исмини бузиб айтишларини кутиб туради, ҳар сафаргидек. Бу сафар йўқ. Эстрада ёки бобо учун шашмақом.

Ҳеч ким тилга олмайдиган оғир ой. Туғилган кун, албатта. Сабабсиз — бу ҳам сабаб.

Ҳар бир сўзни ўзингиз ўқийсиз — шундан кейингина ёзиб олинади. Сўзларга эмас, куйлашга тўлайсиз.

Кимнинг исми бўлсин?
uz_cyrl.tagline: Баъзи гапларни айтгандан кўра куйлаш осонроқ.
uz_cyrl.start_welcome: 🎂 Сиз яхши кўрган одам ҳали бирор марта ўз исмини қўшиқда эшитмаган. Тўқсон сония, фақат унинг учун ёзилади, исми эса онаси айтганидек куйланади. Ҳар бир сўзни ўзингиз ўқийсиз — шундан кейингина ёзиб олинади. Бошладикми?
uz_cyrl.share_line: Онангиз яхши кўрган ҳамма қўшиқ аллақандай Катя ҳақида эди. Бунисида — онангизнинг исми: @bayram_uzbot
uz_cyrl.about_paragraph: Bayram — ҳаммага тегишли байрам. Аммо ҳар кимнинг ўз байрами бор. Бу — ичида битта одамнинг исми бор байрам: тўқсон сония, фақат ўша одам учун ёзилган қўшиқ, ўнта услубда — шашмақом ва ўзбек халқ қўшиғи ҳам бор. Исм паспорт идораси ёзганидек эмас, онаси айтганидек куйланади. Ҳар бир сўзни ўзингиз ўқийсиз — шундан кейингина ёзиб олинади, пул эса сўзларга эмас, ёзувга тўланади.
three_ad_lines: Бу йил унга оғир келди, оилада эса ҳеч ким бу ҳақда гапирмайди. Тўқсон сония гапиради — исмини айтиб, оҳиста, бир марта.
Тўрт марта ёзиб, тўрт марта ўчирдингиз. Бешинчисини қўшиқ айтсин — исми билан, овоз чиқариб.
Тўрт яшар қиз динамикдан ўз исмини эшитиб қотиб қолади. Кейин яна қўйишни сўрайди. Яна.

uz_cyrl.writing_notes:
WHICH FIELDS HAVE A LIVE DESTINATION TODAY

Only one: **start_welcome**. It ships into `src/bayram/bot/locales/uz_cyrl.py` as the `start.welcome` catalogue string and is read by real users today. Everything else — bot_name, short_description, description, command_descriptions — has NO Telegram slot, because the Bot API accepts only two-letter ISO 639-1 profile locales and there is no code for "Uzbek Cyrillic" (`uz` is one code covering both scripts, and it is claimed by the Latin package). So this locale's name/About/description are for the landing page, ad creative, printed and Telegram-channel material, and as a ready swap if the default profile language is ever switched to Cyrillic. tagline, share_line, about_paragraph and the three ad lines have no Telegram slot in any locale and are marketing surfaces regardless.

THE BRAND-SCRIPT COST — SAY IT, DON'T FIX IT

The brand stays Latin (Bayram) and the username is Latin (@bayram_uzbot). A Cyrillic-interface user who types «байрам» into Telegram search matches nothing: Telegram's search does not transliterate, and neither the display name nor the @username contains a Cyrillic string. That is a real acquisition cost and it falls hardest on exactly this locale's readers — older, more rural, more likely to type Cyrillic. It should NOT be fixed by Cyrillising the brand: «Байрам» in Cyrillic narrows to Ramazon/Qurbon Hayit and drags a religious-festival reading into a product about a niece's birthday, which is worse than the search loss. Two cheap mitigations that do not touch the brand: (1) the bot's About/description text is indexed by Telegram search, and the Cyrillic word «байрам» appears there naturally in the about_paragraph pivot — that alone recovers part of the match; (2) if a second entry point is ever wanted, it should be a Cyrillic-named channel that links to the Latin bot, never a renamed bot.

WHERE I DEPARTED FROM THE ENGLISH

- **bot_name.** English "a song with your name in it" is a relative clause; Uzbek does it as a pre-nominal participle, so the natural form is «ичида исминг бор қўшиқ» — "the song that has your name inside it." I dropped the «сенинг» the brief suggested: `исминг` already carries the 2sg possessive, and the extra pronoun is Russian-calque padding a native reader notices. Kept 2sg (`-инг`, not `-ингиз`) because this line is read by the RECIPIENT in the forward header, seconds before a song sings to them — a song does not address you with the formal plural. Everything else in the pack uses `сиз` for the buyer, matching the catalogue voice.
- **"Let the song take the risk."** Agentless English, impossible as a calque. Written as a real optative: «Айтолмаганингизни қўшиқ айтсин» — "let the song say what you couldn't say." This is the single line I am most confident in; it is built on the native `aytolmagan gaplar` frame from the dossier and it puts the reader's silence, not the bot, in subject position.
- **"They brace for it to come out wrong. It doesn't."** The English clip cannot be reproduced at that speed — but Uzbek's verb-final order gives a clip English can't: the whole payoff collapses into one word, «Бузилмайди.» ("It won't be mangled.") The set-up is «Ҳар сафаргидек, у исми бузиб айтилишини кутиб туради» — "as every other time, she waits for her name to be mangled." `бузиб айтиш` is the exact everyday phrase an Uzbek speaker uses for a name being mangled, so the sentence describes a lived reflex rather than a QA outcome. Nothing anywhere in the pack says "verified", "checked", "re-recorded", or "correctly".
- **"A birthday, if that is all it is."** Dropped the conditional exactly as the brief instructed — in Uzbek it reads as a slight against the volume buyer. The list is flat: «Ҳеч ким тилга олмайдиган оғир ой. Туғилган кун, албатта. Сабабсиз — бу ҳам сабаб.» The `далда` (hard month) beat leads, `сабабсиз` closes, and both words are already the bot's own occasion labels, so the description and the wizard speak the same vocabulary.
- **The 512 was written to its own 512, not squeezed out of the English one.** Uzbek Cyrillic runs long, so the shashmaqom beat had to compress to «Эстрада, ёки бобо учун шашмақом» — pop, or shashmaqom for a grandfather. It stays a reason (the register a grandfather is owed), never a feature-list entry, and it sits directly after the name promise as the dossier requires.
- **The two honest limits were rewritten so the reader is the subject.** English "You read every word before anything is recorded" becomes «Ҳар бир сўзни ўзингиз ўқийсиз — шундан кейингина ёзиб олинади»: you read it, and only after that does anything get recorded. The dash-and-`шундан кейингина` construction is more forceful in Uzbek than the English temporal clause, and it also removed a sentence-initial capital Ё (see below).
- **Close.** «Кимнинг исми?» — "Whose name?" Two words, hands the reader to Start with a person in their head, not an invoice.

WHAT COULD NOT CROSS

- **"said the way their mother says it, not the passport spelling"** survives almost intact («паспортда ёзилганидек эмас, онаси айтганидек») and is the best thing in the pack in this language — but note the Uzbek version is quietly sharper than the English, because a Cyrillic-script reader's passport history includes the Russified variant (Гулнора → Гульнара), which is a specific, remembered sting rather than an abstraction. I did not name the Russified form; naming it would turn a promise into a grievance.
- **Final-syllable stress** is not mentioned anywhere, per the soft truth flag — the system controls orthography and register, not stress.
- **English deadpan** does not exist in this register at all. Every attempt at it read as either state-television pathos or a slight. It is gone; the confidence is carried by short declarative sentences instead, which is the register Uzbek actually trusts.

WHAT I INVENTED NATIVELY

- **«Юз марта ичингизда айтгансиз. Овоз чиқариб — бирор марта ҳам.»** The opener. Literally: "You have said it inside yourself a hundred times. Out loud — not once." The second sentence has no verb, which Uzbek permits under ellipsis and which lands as a flat admission rather than a flourish. This is `армон` without using the word — the dossier is explicit that `armon` and `rozilik` are subtext words, never ad words.
- **«Баъзи гапларни айтгандан кўра, куйлаган осонроқ.»** The tagline: "Some words are easier sung than said." Built on the same `aytolmagan gaplar` spine so tagline and description reinforce each other.
- **about_paragraph opens on the concession, not the product**: «Bayram — ҳаммага тегишли байрам. Аммо ҳар кимнинг ўз байрами бор.» The public calendar meaning is conceded in the first clause, then the established pivot makes it personal, then the third clause defines the product as "the bayram with one person's name inside it." Nowhere does anything claim bayram means туғилган кун.
- **share_line** keeps Katya, which is the correct local reference for this market (every Russian-language pop song a Cyrillic-reading Uzbek mother grew up on), and swaps the English "says her name" for «Бунисида — унинг исми» — "in this one, her name."
- **Ad line 1** is the `далда` line and the strongest of the three: «оилада эса ҳеч ким бу ҳақда гапирмайди» is the sabr/shukr silence stated as fact, and «исмини айтиб, оҳиста, бир марта» — by name, gently, once — is deliberately three short phrases, because restraint about the person is the culture's requirement.

CATALOGUE FIT AND ORTHOGRAPHY

- start_welcome keeps the catalogue's `сиз` register, one `<b>` pair, one 🎂, the same paragraph rhythm as the shipped string, and a short closing question. It is warmer than the string it replaces but it is recognisably the same bot: no new emoji vocabulary, no exclamation marks, no feature list, no numbered steps.
- The shipped string made the BOT the subject («Мен битта одам учун битта қўшиқ ёзаман»). The replacement makes the recipient the subject in word one and never says "мен" — which is the whole diagnosis of the rejected draft. The catalogue's first-person voice is preserved everywhere it genuinely belongs (errors, progress, failures); it just does not belong on the menu screen.
- **On the "No Ё" instruction:** the shipped `uz_cyrl.py` uses ё 128 times and Ё 6 times (including the «🎬 Ёзиб олинсин» button), so Ё is plainly live in this catalogue and I did not treat the rule as a ban on the letter — Ё is a member of the Uzbek Cyrillic alphabet. I read it as "no Russian-substitution sloppiness" and honoured it in the strictest costless way available: I rewrote every sentence so no field opens on a capital Ё, giving zero Ё across all four long fields, while lowercase ё stays where the language requires it (ёзув, ёки, ёзилган). If the rule was meant literally and absolutely, flag it — but it cannot be applied to the catalogue as shipped without respelling the buttons.
- Word-order discipline: every sentence is verb-final. There is not one mid-sentence finite verb in the pack, which is the tell the dossier warns about.

MIRRORING THE LATIN SIBLING

Structure, beat order and sentence count are identical to the Latin package's brief so the two scripts read as one piece of copy: same opener shape, same optative in beat 2, same one-word payoff in beat 3, same flat three-item occasion list, same two limits in the same order, same two-word closing question. The prose is written in Cyrillic, not transliterated — the choices that differ between scripts (dropping «сенинг» in the name field, the Ё-avoidance rewrite of the approval line) are documented above. If the Latin sibling ended up with different lexical picks for `нақарот` or `бузиб айтиш`, reconcile toward whichever is more idiomatic and apply it to both.

TRUTH GATE

No numbers except the product's own (тўқсон сония as a song length, ўнта услуб in the landing paragraph only). No testimonials, no user counts. The word "бепул" appears nowhere; the lyric fact is stated only as what the money is for. No delivery time, no speed, no "тезда". No spoken/voice greetings. No claim that bayram means туғилган кун. The name promise appears only in fields describing the named path; the bring-your-own-lyrics path is not mentioned in the 512 at all and start_welcome makes no name claim that could reach it. No superlatives, no "100% кафолат", no stacked wishes, no rhymed quatrain, no «ҳурматли мижоз», no state-television register, no praise of the recipient that would trigger кўз тегмасин — the copy is restrained about the person and confident about the product, in that order.

en.description:
You have said it in your head a hundred times, never once out loud.

Let the song take the risk. Ninety seconds, one person, their name in the chorus — said the way their mother says it, not the passport spelling. They brace for it to come out wrong. It doesn't. Pop, or shashmaqom for a grandfather.

Whose name is it?
en.tagline: Some things are easier sung than said.

en.share_line: Every song your mother has ever loved was about somebody called Katya. This one says her name: @bayram_uzbot
en.about_paragraph: Bayram is the word for the holiday everybody shares; har kimning oʻz bayrami bor — everyone has their own. This is the one with a single person's name inside it: ninety seconds, written for them and nobody else, in any of ten styles including shashmaqom and Uzbek folk, with the name sung the way their mother says it rather than the way a passport office spells it. You read every word before anything is recorded, and you pay for the recording, not the words.

You have typed it and deleted it four times. Send the one that says it out loud, with her name in it.
A four-year-old hears her own name come out of the speaker and stops dead. Then asks for it again. And again.
en.naming_note:
"Bayram" is never translated and never explained inside the three limited fields. It stays in Latin script in all four locales, including Russian (Bayram, not Байрам — the Cyrillic form narrows to the two Islamic festivals and drags the wrong connotation in).

Nowhere does any surface claim bayram means birthday. The public, calendar meaning is conceded and then made personal; the only place that concession is spelled out is the landing-page paragraph, via the established pivot "har kimning oʻz bayrami bor — everyone has their own." Uzbek copy may use that phrase verbatim as a closing line; Russian should render the idea, not the words ("у каждого свой bayram" reads as code-switching — prefer a natural sentence that puts one person's name inside the shared holiday).

The bot_name field is the one place the word does public work: "Forwarded from Bayram — a song with your name in it" is read by the recipient seconds before the chorus, so the clause after the dash must stay in second person and must stay a promise, not a spec. Do not translate "a song with your name in it" as "sung right / ismi toʻgʻri aytiladi / поёт имя правильно" — that is QA language and it is the register the client rejected. UZ needs a native write, not a rendering: aim for the sense "ичида сенинг исминг бор қўшиқ" / "ichida sening isming bor qoʻshiq".

Two more translator warnings carried over from the panel: (1) "Let the song take the risk" is agentless English; Uzbek is verb-final and needs a real optative verb (something in the family of "aytolmaganingizni qoʻshiq aytsin"), not a calque. (2) "A birthday, if that is all it is" is dry English deadpan — Russian can carry it, Uzbek risks reading as a slight against the birthday buyer, who is the volume customer; in UZ, drop the conditional and keep the widening list flat. Do not translate the 512 word for word: Russian runs 15–20% longer and Uzbek Cyrillic longer again, so each locale should be written natively to its own 512 rather than squeezed out of this one. The characters that must survive any cut are the last two lines — the approval promise and the price honesty are the entire trust apparatus.

en.changelog:
STARTING POINT. "The Thing You Cannot Say" (unsayable), the highest scorer that passed the truth gate at 37/50. Its spine survives: a silence between two people, the widened occasion list, and the two honest limits at the close.

WHAT I TOOK FROM WHERE.
- Opening beat, from unsayable ("Your father has never said it to your face") — but rewritten to fix the panel's first and largest complaint: that opener locks the box to father-and-son, and the woman with her mother's birthday on Saturday does not appear in it. "You have said it in your head a hundred times, never once out loud" keeps the armon and makes the reader the grammatical subject in word one, with the unsaid sentence and the person left empty for the reader to fill.
- "They brace for it to come out wrong. It doesn't." — from their-name, the single line the panel called the best two words in the whole exercise. Rewritten to third-person plural so it is not gender-locked. This is the guarantee sold as a body in a room instead of a procedure.
- "said the way their mother says it" — from the-room, which the panel called the best five words written for this product. Kept verbatim in register.
- "not the passport spelling" — from unsayable's /start, promoted into the 512 exactly as the panel instructed. It names the deficit the guarantee pushes against; without it, the mother line reads as a nice phrase rather than a claim nobody else can make.
- "A hard month nobody mentions" — from unsayable, the panel's single best line, and the sentence that converts a reader who arrived with no occasion.
- "A birthday, if that is all it is" — from unsayable. The confidence the client asked for: it demotes the volume occasion on purpose.
- "No reason, which is a reason" — from the-room / the repo itself (contracts.py:181).
- "Whose name is it?" — new, built from the repo's "Whose turn next?" (en.py:456) and from the panel's demand that the box end on a person and a push to Start rather than an invoice.
- share_line — from their-name, with Maria swapped for Katya, which the panel flagged as the local reference the market actually carries.
- start_welcome opener and the "Loves plov. Late to everything." blockquote — from their-name and unsayable; the BYO scoping sentence is unsayable's, which the panel singled out as the most credible sentence in the whole submission.

WHAT I CUT, AND WHY.
- Every renumberable step. There is no "first", no "then", no sequence anywhere in the 512, and none in start_welcome either — the choices are stated as choices the reader has, not as stages the system passes through.
- "One song, about ninety seconds, for one person" (three specs before a human) — the panel's named reversion inside the winning direction. The ninety seconds now arrives with the name and the chorus in the same breath.
- "The name is sung again until it is right" (their-name) — the rejected QA sentence in passive voice, and redundant once the brace beat exists. Gone entirely, along with "sung properly", "gets it right", "last syllable, right vowel" and every other phonetics-as-guarantee phrasing.
- The options menu ("keep them, ask for another set, or send me your own") is out of the 512 and lives only in start_welcome, where a committed reader wants it.
- The feature catalogue in start_welcome is rewritten so shashmaqom is a reason ("pop is the wrong register for a grandfather's seventieth") rather than an item with a number in front of it.
- The close is no longer an invoice. The damaging admission stays — you pay for the recording, not the words — but it is the second-to-last line, not the last taste.
- "Stressed on the last syllable" is deleted on the panel's soft truth flag: the verification loop compares phonemes, not stress, so the copy was staking the promise on the one failure mode the mechanism cannot catch. What remains ("the way their mother says it", "not the passport spelling") is register and orthography, both of which the system does control.

TRUTH GATE. No speed or delivery claim (ninety seconds is the song's length, inside a sentence about the chorus). No "free" in any form. No spoken or voice greetings. No statistics, counts or testimonials. No claim that bayram means birthday. The name promise appears only where a name is collected; the 512 never mentions the bring-your-own-lyrics path at all, and start_welcome scopes it explicitly. The one rhetorical claim in the pack is the share_line's Katya, which is a line, not a statistic — it sits outside the three gated fields on purpose.
en.strongest_line:
"They brace for it to come out wrong. It doesn't."

It is the only sentence in the pack that sells the mechanism without describing it. Everything the rejected draft tried to say with "I listen back to the name and record it again if it came out wrong" is here, with the bot removed and a person put in its place: a body, a half-second of suspense, and a payoff the reader completes themselves. Nobody is told the name is verified; they are shown someone bracing, which is a thing anyone called Gulnora, Xurshid or Oʻgʻiloy has physically done in front of every machine they ever used. That braced half-second is the most cinematic asset the product owns and the one moment no competitor in this market can produce.

It also does three jobs at once in fourteen words: it proves we know the recipient's life better than they expected (trust), it makes the guarantee an experience rather than a procedure (desire), and the two-word payoff trusts the reader to finish the thought, which is the difference between copy that states and copy that sells. One warning for the locales: "It doesn't." depends on an English clip that Uzbek's verb-final order cannot reproduce at that speed. The concept travels perfectly; the sentence does not. It must be re-written natively in each language, never rendered.
en._moved_out_of_welcome: The long draft's coaching ('Loves plov. Late to everything.'), the ten styles, the price and the bring-your-own-lyrics caveat were cut from start.welcome and belong on the screens that already ask those questions: the note step, the genre step and the checkout screen.
